newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan police shut 188 sex parlours in raid.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan police shut 188 sex parlours in raid.

text.p: Taiwan police, fighting a "war against prostitution", said on Tuesday they have shut down 188 sex parlours in capital Taipei in the past seven days, and vowed to bust the remaining 103 by the end of the day.

"We have cut off water and power supplies to a total of 188 sex parlours and forced them to close, and we have 103 to go before the end of today," Taipei police chief Ting Yuan-ching told city mayor Chen Shui-bian in a public conference.
Chen, who had demanded that the police shut all of Taipei's bustling sex establishments in one week, said his war on vice would not be a success until remaining parlours were closed.
"The remaining 103 sex parlours need to close down by the end of today," Chen said.
Many of the sex parlours hire teenage girls as "public relation managers" to provide sex service to clients.
Local newspapers said their salaries could reach as much as T$2 million (US$72,700) a month.
Ting said his department has already pinned down 69 of the 103 remaining parlours, and would raid them on Tuesday night.
"We are confident we can get to the 69 and then the rest before the day is over," he said.
A police spokesman declined to reveal how many people had been arrested in the crackdown, saying a final tally would not be released until the entire operation was over.

Chen, who in 1994 became the first member of an opposition party to be elected Taipei mayor, has said he would make it a priority of his administration to rid the capital city of its notorious red-light districts.
